LAND ACQUISITION OFFICER,
BENGALURU DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY, BENGALURU VIDE ANNEXURE-A AND QUASH THE SAME AS ILLEGAL, WITHOUT AUTHORITY OF LAW AND PASSED IN GROSS VIOLATION OF PRINCIPLES OF NATURAL JUSTICE AND HENCE NULL AND VOID AND ETC.,
 -4-  NC: 2023:KHC:32415  WP No. 52091 of 2018  THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER
The limited question involved in this petition is a dispute with regard to the disbursement of the compensation.

Learned counsel for the petitioners, drawing attention to this Court to Annexure-Q produced at page No.100 of the petition, submits that the objections in the form of representation submitted by the petitioners on 16.09.2015, along with the necessary documents enclosed with the said representation, were duly served on the respondents authorities on 16.09.2015 instant.
It is Smt Venkatalakshmamma vs The State Of Karnataka

3 further submitted that, not-withstanding the submission of said representation, the respondent authorities, without even adjudicating upon the same or passing necessary orders under Section 30 of the Land Acquisition Act, proceeded to disburse the compensation amount, constraining the petitioner to approach this Court seeking the relief as sought for in the petition.

In response, Sri.Gowtham Dev C. Ullal, learned counsel appearing for the respondent authority,
submits that the said representation was submitted at the tappal section and that the same has missed the attention of the Respondent authority while passing the orders resulting in the disbursement of the compensation amount.
However, he fairly submits that the Respondent authorities will consider the representation produced with the petition at Annexure-Q given an opportunity.
3. The submission is taken on record.

4. In view of the aforesaid submissions, the following:
ORDER i.

The writ petition is disposed of, directing the respondent-SLAO to pass appropriate orders on the representation vide Annexure-Q, dated 16.09.2015,
including passing orders under Section 30 of the Land Acquisition Act and referring the NC: 2023:KHC:32415 matter to the reference Court, if required, to the extent of the claim of the petitioner within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
ii. The respondent-SLAO shall also ensure that the concerned parties are heard with prior notice in the matter.

Sd/-
